# Oklahoma City Thunder 2026/27 Season Outlook

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-07-26, 40:57. https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM

## Summary

Josh Lloyd and Ryland Styles of Locked On Thunder preview the Oklahoma City Thunder's 2026/27 season. They focus on health, especially Jalen Williams and Ajay Mitchell, and on the offseason exits of Lu Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins. Those trades were made mainly to cut the luxury tax bill, with unproven rookies and young players coming in as replacements. Ryland expects a step back in the regular season to about 62 wins, with OKC and San Antonio still the top two seeds in the West. Other topics are Cason Wallace's role as the likely starter in Dort's spot, Ajay Mitchell's shooting splits as a starter versus off the bench, the team's internal belief in Jared McCain, and Chet Holmgren bouncing back from a poor series. Both hosts note how few threes the Thunder's core players take, and Ryland says the team may push them to shoot more.

## Rules and methods

- [2:44](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=164) The number of games played can overstate a player's real healthy sample. Many of Jalen Williams' 40 games were limited-minute games while he recovered from injuries.
  > "it was probably 20 full speed games and that had a huge impact across the team"
- [4:16](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=256) Losing depth hurts a team more in the regular season than in the playoffs, because playoff rotations shrink to eight or nine players.
  > "They'll have to shrink their rotation like a normal team would to like nine or eight guys"
- [21:59](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=1319) Big men with a history of repeated lower body injuries rarely see those problems go away.
  > "bigs who have constantly had lower body injuries, historically speaking, those don't just up and go away"
- [34:14](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=2054) A player's shooting efficiency depends on lineup context. Playing next to stars who draw defenders creates more open looks than playing as the lone creator on a bench unit.
  > "the shots that he's being funneled are generated by Shay and they're generated by these guys who have better gravity"
- [36:07](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=2167) A good three-point percentage on low volume does not make a reliable shooter. Volume of around five or six attempts per game, or a high share of shots from three, is needed.
  > "if you are going to be a very good shooter it needs to be more than that"
- [37:38](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=2258) Shot quality is player-specific. A contested mid-range shot can be efficient for an elite mid-range shooter and a bad shot for others.
  > "each guy has a different uh way to grade efficient shots"
